items.regeneration: Electrochemical oxidation at ambient temperature: Faradaic efficiency 79.6 +/- 3.8%, energy 106.9 kJ/mol CO2 (2.43 GJ/t electricity, cell level). OptiLex floor: 0.212 V for a one-electron-per-CO2 carrier. For comparison, aqueous Alizarin Red S has a theoretical minimum of 24.6 kJ/mol and ran 100 cycles/205 h (ChemSusChem 2025, doi 10.1002/cssc.202401315).
items.stability_and_lifetime: 48 cycles in air with negligible carrier degradation. Quinones show an inherent trade-off: structures more tolerant of O2 bind CO2 more weakly (ChemPhysChem 2026, doi 10.1002/cphc.202500472); a benzodithiophene quinone ran over 100 h at 13% CO2 with 3.5% O2 at electron utilisation 0.83 (Angew 2024, doi 10.1002/anie.202412229; flue-gas conditions, not DAC).
items.cost: Not reported; electrode volumetric capacity 1.1 kg CO2/m3 implies large electrode volume per tonne.
items.trl_and_scale: TRL 3; coin/flow-cell scale. Earlier faradaic electro-swing reports of 40-90 kJ/mol were at 15% CO2 feed or produced dilute product.
items.bottleneck: Oxygen side-reactions (21% O2 vs 0.04% CO2 is a 500:1 excess) and low volumetric capacity; O2-tolerance trades directly against CO2 affinity.

items.name: Electrochemical pH-swing release with staged or mediated proton transfer
items.mechanism: Air is contacted with alkaline liquid; CO2 is then released by electrochemically lowering pH. Staging the pH drop (hydrogen loop from pH 13.5 to 9, then a MnO2 proton-sponge electrode for bicarbonate) or using proton-coupled electron-transfer mediators cuts the Nernst voltage penalty.
items.uptake_and_conditions: Capture step is conventional hydroxide/carbonate absorption. Integrated eDAC with local hydroxide generation at a gas-diffusion electrode: capture efficiency 36-47% at 2 mA/cm2 and about 40% up to 10 mA/cm2 on 400 ppm CO2 (Nat Commun 2026, doi 10.1038/s41467-026-74879-z).
items.regeneration: Two-stage release from post-capture liquid measured at about 4.5 GJ/t CO2 (2.4 GJ H2-loop stage + 2.1 GJ MnO2 stage), vs at least 10 GJ/t for bipolar-membrane electrodialysis (PNAS 2026; release step only, electricity). Integrated eDAC: 17.8-25.8 GJ/t at 4-25 mA/cm2 when mediator regeneration is paired with oxygen evolution; 4-10.9 GJ/t if paired with glycerol oxidation. AQDS dual-electrolyser: 257 kJ/mol = 5.8 GJ/t (RSC Adv 2026, doi 10.1039/d5ra09310d).
items.stability_and_lifetime: Integrated eDAC stable over 50 h; a porous-solid-electrolyte reactor ran DAC for over 2,000 h at over 93% removal and 30 mA/cm2 (Nat Commun 2025, doi 10.1038/s41467-025-65332-8; energy per tonne not extracted).
items.cost: eDAC authors: cutting electricity from $0.05 to $0.01/kWh at 25 mA/cm2 saves $287/t, i.e. about 7,200 kWh/t at that operating point.
items.trl_and_scale: TRL 3-4 in papers; company pilots (RepAir, Mission Zero) listed at TRL 6 in the 2025 Energy Environ Sci review.
items.bottleneck: Measured full-system electricity is 4.5-26 GJ/t, i.e. 4-10% second-law efficiency at the high end; current densities 2-30 mA/cm2 vs over 100 mA/cm2 in industrial cells.

items.name: Magnetic induction swing adsorption (Fe3O4/SBA-15-PEI)
items.mechanism: Magnetite nanoparticles embedded in an amine-loaded silica heat the sorbent from the inside in an alternating magnetic field; the trigger is still heat, delivered volumetrically and fast.
items.uptake_and_conditions: 1.53 mmol/g at 30 C, 500 ppm CO2 in Ar (1.21 without Fe3O4); 2.05 mmol/g at 30% RH with pre-humidification; 3.2 mmol/g at 90% RH (ACS Appl Mater Interfaces 2025, abstract only).
items.regeneration: Heating/cooling 12.5/22.7 C/min dry and 5.0/11.6 C/min humid, 328%/483% and 138%/218% faster than conventional thermal swing; desorbed 1.25 mmol/g dry (92.6%) and 3.24 mmol/g humid (99.9%). No GJ/t or coil efficiency in the abstract.
items.stability_and_lifetime: About 1.46 mmol/g maintained over 10 humid DAC cycles.
items.cost: Not reported.
items.trl_and_scale: TRL 3. A related Fe3O4@Mg-MOF-74 composite reached only 0.60 mmol/g at 1.2 bar (ACS Omega 2026).
items.bottleneck: No measured electricity per tonne; induction delivers electricity as heat, so it can only win through cycle time (capital), not energy.

items.name: Microwave/dielectric regeneration of ionic-liquid and zeolite sorbents
items.mechanism: Microwaves couple directly to polar ionic-liquid sorbents (amino-acid anions), heating the sorbent volume rather than the vessel and shortening exposure to hot oxygen.
items.uptake_and_conditions: Ionic liquid [N4444][Tau+Lys] designed for DAC; capacity not in abstract (Environ Sci Technol 2026, abstract only).
items.regeneration: Versus conventional heating: maximum desorption rate up about 496%, recovered CO2 up about 66%, input energy 0.26 kWh vs 0.69 kWh per experiment (about 62% lower). Not normalised per tonne in the abstract.
items.stability_and_lifetime: Earlier imidazolium cyanopyrrolide ionic liquid lost 50% capacity after 7 days in O2 at 80 C with conventional heating, while microwave regeneration at 80-100 C showed no measurable degradation (ChemSusChem 2023, doi 10.1002/cssc.202300118).
items.cost: Not reported.
items.trl_and_scale: TRL 2-3; bench.
items.bottleneck: Benefit shown is kinetic and per-experiment; no per-tonne energy with pure CO2 product; magnetron efficiency not included.

items.name: Liquid-to-solid phase-change absorbents (isophorone diamine carbamic acid; biphasic ionic liquids)
items.mechanism: A liquid amine captures CO2 and the product precipitates as a solid, which pulls the equilibrium toward capture; release happens from the re-dissolved state, where CO2 is held more weakly. Solubility, not only temperature, sets the binding strength.
items.uptake_and_conditions: Isophorone diamine (IPDA): over 99% CO2 removal from a 400 ppm flow sustained for 100 h, CO2:amine ratio at least 1:1, capture rate 201 mmol/h per mol amine (ACS Environ Au 2022). Biphasic ionic liquid with MgO nanoparticles: 0.65 mol/mol total loading, 79.5% of CO2 concentrated in a solid phase that is 15.1% of system mass (Environ Sci Technol 2026, doi 10.1021/acs.est.5c16348, abstract only).
items.regeneration: IPDA: complete desorption at 60 C (333 K) in water/DMSO and from 50 C in methanol, measured under N2 flow; more than half released at 60 C without gas flow in methanol (ACS Omega 2024, doi 10.1021/acsomega.4c05978). Biphasic ionic liquid: claimed 0.94 GJ/t. OptiLex check: 0.94 GJ/t is 41 kJ/mol; as heat at 100 C it carries 8.3 kJ/mol of exergy, below the 20.5 kJ/mol floor for pure CO2, so the figure cannot be a complete cycle to pure CO2 unless heat is supplied above about 317 C or other inputs are uncounted.
items.stability_and_lifetime: IPDA reused over repeated cycles without reported degradation and 100 h continuous capture; biphasic ionic liquid over 96.5% retention across 7 cycles.
items.cost: Not reported.
items.trl_and_scale: TRL 3; millilitre to bench flow.
items.bottleneck: Low-temperature release shown under inert purge or in volatile methanol (boiling point 65 C); solid handling; energy claims not on a pure-CO2 basis.

items.name: Carbonic anhydrase and synthetic mimics for capture kinetics
items.mechanism: The enzyme catalyses CO2 hydration to bicarbonate, letting benign low-enthalpy carbonate or amino-acid solvents absorb as fast as caustic hydroxide. It changes kinetics (contactor size), not thermodynamics (regeneration energy).
items.uptake_and_conditions: Immobilised enzyme hydrogel packings tested with 10 vol% CO2 (not air) in 10 wt% K2CO3 at pH 10.5, ambient temperature (Gels 2023). No measured rate data at 400 ppm were found for 2022-2026; a 2026 'enzymatic DAC' membrane paper screened supports without enzyme. OptiLex film-theory calc: uncatalysed pH 10 carbonate has K_L 0.04 mm/s; 0.1-1 g/L of enzyme at 1.5e8 /M/s gives 1.0-3.1 mm/s (24-76 times), comparable to 1 M hydroxide (4.0 mm/s ideal; about 1.3 mm/s measured in real contactor liquor).
items.regeneration: Unchanged by the enzyme. OptiLex equilibrium calc: a 1-2 M K2CO3 solution can only reach 9-12% bicarbonate conversion before its CO2 back-pressure hits a quarter to half of ambient, i.e. 0.09-0.18 mol CO2 per litre cyclic loading, so a non-thermal release step (electrochemical, crystallisation) is required.
items.stability_and_lifetime: After 1,032 h continuous alkaline flow: 52% of initial capture performance and 34% of the enzyme contribution retained; over 87% activity after 150 days of washing/testing. Textile packings: 100% of initial efficiency over 71 days and 500 h scrubber run (Catalysts 2022, doi 10.3390/catal12101108).
items.cost: Not reported for DAC.
items.trl_and_scale: Enzyme-carbonate capture reached pilot scale for flue gas; TRL 2-3 for DAC.
items.bottleneck: Solves only the contactor; cyclic loading of carbonate at 42 Pa is about 0.1-0.2 mol/L and enzyme contribution decays by two-thirds in 43 days.

items.name: Bis-iminoguanidine crystallisation with peptide/amino-acid absorbents
items.mechanism: An aqueous amino acid or peptide absorbs CO2; a guanidine then crystallises it as an insoluble hydrogen-bonded carbonate salt, regenerating the absorbent at ambient temperature. Only the small mass of crystals is heated.
items.uptake_and_conditions: Theoretical capacity of isolated carbonate solids 2.1-6.1 mmol/g depending on guanidine; 89% crystallisation yield over 10 cycles for GBIG with a flue-gas simulant (Chem Sci 2021 perspective summarising 2017-2021 primary work).
items.regeneration: Crystals release CO2 and water at 80-120 C under N2 purge. Measured regeneration energies: 151.5 kJ/mol (3.4 GJ/t) for GBIG, 323-358 kJ/mol for MGBIG phases, 422 kJ/mol (9.6 GJ/t) for DABIG, largely from hydrate water.
items.stability_and_lifetime: 10 cycles with quantitative guanidine recovery in the cited tests; long-term data not given.
items.cost: Not reported.
items.trl_and_scale: TRL 3-4.
items.bottleneck: Each carbonate crystal carries 2-4 waters of hydration whose removal dominates the energy; small structural changes shift regeneration energy by a factor of 2.8.

bottlenecks: Thermodynamic coupling is only partly breakable. OptiLex Hill-isotherm calc (dS -165 J/mol/K, unload 90% to 10% at 1 kPa CO2): a Langmuir sorbent needs 126 C and 3.83 GJ/t (reaction + sensible, no water); a cooperative sorbent with Hill coefficient 4 needs 78 C and 2.72 GJ/t; an infinitely sharp step needs 63 C. Cooperativity removes the isotherm-width term but not the pressure-ratio term: delivering pure CO2 at 1 atm still needs 142 C at dH -68.4 kJ/mol.

Purge-gas confound in almost every 'low-temperature release' result (TriH, IPDA, charged-sorbents, induction, guanidines were all regenerated under N2 or Ar). OptiLex calc for dH -70 kJ/mol: unloading to 20% needs 59 C at 100 Pa CO2 but 92 C at 1 kPa, 132 C at 10 kPa and 183 C at 100 kPa. A result measured under inert purge says nothing about producing concentrated CO2.

Capacity, not binding strength, is the measured lever on energy. Sensible heat at an 80 C swing is 3.75 GJ/t at 0.5 mol/kg, 1.80 at 1.04 mol/kg and 0.30 at 6.2 mol/kg (OptiLex calc). Measured extremes match: charged-sorbents at 0.08-0.14 mol/kg need 6.5-11.4 GJ/t of electricity; the 6.57 mmol/g amine aerogel needs 3.4 GJ/t.

Water. Each mol of water co-desorbed per mol CO2 adds 1.0 GJ/t. A cooperative MOF (mmen-Mg2(dobpdc)) holds 1.5 mol CO2/kg but up to 40 mol H2O/kg at 90% RH (up to 26.7 GJ/t if co-desorbed). Moisture swing needs at least 3.2 mol H2O per mol CO2 at 30% RH and 10.8 at 70% RH to reach a 2 kPa product (reversible limit); practical 10-100 mol/mol means 4-41 t water per t CO2.

Photon economy for photo-swing: one photon (230-328 kJ/mol) per CO2 against a 20.5 kJ/mol floor caps efficiency below 9%; best measured yields are 0.125 CO2/photon (visible, 15% CO2 feed) and 4% quantum yield (UV photobase), giving 48-186 GJ/t of light and 27-517 m2-yr of collector per tonne, vs 1.2-4.5 m2-yr/t for photovoltaics driving a conventional cycle.

Electricity delivered as heat (Joule, induction, microwave) costs more exergy than heat-pump or waste heat: 3.4 GJ/t electrical is 944 kWh/t ($47/t at $50/MWh) vs 559 kWh/t ($28/t) for the 6.04 GJ/t reference cycle on a COP-3 heat pump. These triggers can only pay through faster cycles: doubling cycles per day saves $68-137/t of the $274/t capital charge, depending on how much capital scales with sorbent throughput.

Demonstrated lifetimes are 1-3 orders of magnitude short. Cycles shown: 6 (photobase), about 10 (TriH, induction, vapour-promoted), 40 (hydrogel), 48 (redox carrier in air), 100-500 (amine aerogel), 150 (charged-sorbent, at 30% CO2). OptiLex needs about 20,000 cycles for $22/t at $20/kg and 1 mol/kg. The one 300-day outdoor moisture-swing record shows loss of functional groups (UV), nitrate competition and biofouling; enzyme packings kept 52% of performance after 1,032 h.

Oxygen for redox triggers: air has about 500 times more O2 than CO2. Measured Faradaic efficiency under air is 79.6% for the best O2-shielded carrier, and quinone families show an inherent trade-off between O2 tolerance and CO2 affinity. Measured electrochemical DAC electricity spans 2.4 GJ/t (cell level, ionic-liquid electrolyte) through 4.5 GJ/t (release step only) to 17.8-25.8 GJ/t (integrated system with oxygen evolution).

Carbonic anhydrase fixes kinetics only: 0.1-1 g/L could lift a pH-10 carbonate film coefficient from 0.04 to 1-3 mm/s (OptiLex film-theory calc), but carbonate solutions at DAC back-pressure cycle only 0.09-0.18 mol CO2/L and still need a separate release step; no measured 400 ppm enzyme kinetics were found for 2022-2026.
open_problems: Humidity-tolerant cooperativity: design a step-isotherm sorbent whose step survives 50-80% RH, or one where water is a required partner in the cooperative unit (as in TriH, where water lowers the barrier). Test: measured Hill coefficient of the 400 ppm isotherm at 20%, 50%, 80% RH, plus mol H2O co-adsorbed per mol CO2. Verifier target: n of at least 4 retained and under 2 mol H2O per mol CO2.

Non-volatile, non-melting analogues of the TriH phase-change triamine (salts, oligomers, tethered or co-crystallised forms) that keep over 4 mmol/g in humid air. Conventional core (polyamine carbamate chemistry) plus one imported mechanism (crystal engineering of a switchable network solid). Kill test: vapour pressure at 100 C and capacity after 1,000 cycles.

Cheap route to 1:1 amine-to-CO2 stoichiometry: reproduce the proton-acceptor (proton-trap) effect of the N5-dGA aerogel on low-cost conductive carbons instead of 1600 C graphene aerogel with plasma treatment, and replicate the 6.57 mmol/g, 3.4 GJ/t result independently with a pure-CO2 product.

A purge-free regeneration benchmark: re-rank published 'low-temperature' sorbents by the temperature and energy needed to release into at least 50 kPa CO2. This is a calculation-plus-literature task the idea engine can execute with sorbent.py and would expose which unconventional triggers survive.

Solubility (solvent) swing as a deliberate decoupling trick: capture as an insoluble solid, release from a state where the adduct is weakly bound (the IPDA carbamic-acid system does this with methanol or DMSO). Open question: a non-volatile, oxidation-stable solvent pair, and a full energy balance including solid-liquid separation and solvent losses.

Pair carbonic anhydrase or a robust zinc mimic with a sorbent whose bottleneck is kinetics rather than thermodynamics: bicarbonate-forming moisture-swing sorbents, or carbonate/amino-acid liquids regenerated by staged electrochemical pH swing (2.1 GJ/t measured for the bicarbonate stage). Also catalyse the release side: a catalytic membrane-vacuum study reported up to 64.4% higher desorption flux and 39.1% lower thermal energy (Small 2025, doi 10.1002/smll.202503023).

Moisture swing that survives outdoors and releases below saturation: UV-stable and nitrate-tolerant cationic sites, regeneration at 80% RH or less (the LCST hydrogel reaches 79%), with measured mol H2O per mol CO2 and product CO2 partial pressure reported, which current papers omit.

Break the O2-tolerance versus CO2-affinity trade-off in redox carriers by design of the gas-transport layer rather than the molecule, in an aqueous or solid electrolyte instead of an ionic liquid, at over 1,000 cycles in real air.

Volumetric heating (induction, microwave, Joule) judged on capital, not energy: measure cycles per day and kWh per tonne with pure CO2 product, heating only the sorbent (near-zero inert mass). Target from OptiLex: at least 2 times the cycle rate at no more than about 950 kWh/t.

Photo-swing kill criterion: only pursue if a visible-light photoswitch can deliver at least 0.5 CO2 per photon at molar concentration over 1,000 cycles; otherwise photovoltaics plus a heat pump uses 6-100 times less land. A screening calculation over known photoacid/photobase families could settle this cheaply.

key_claims.claim: A defect-engineered, amine-loaded conductive graphene aerogel (N5-dGA) captured 6.57 mmol CO2 per gram from 400 ppm CO2 at 25 C and 80% RH (2.93 mmol/g dry) and was regenerated by Joule heating to 80 C with a reported heat duty of 3.4 GJ per tonne CO2, losing 3.7% of uptake after 100 cycles (Nat Commun 2026, bench scale, single group). If it replicates with a pure-CO2 product, raising capacity through 1:1 amine-to-CO2 stoichiometry is the most effective measured way to cut regeneration energy among the unconventional triggers.

In diamine-appended metal-organic frameworks at direct-air-capture conditions, adsorbed water shifts CO2 binding from cooperative chains to non-cooperative sites, so the step-shaped isotherm seen in dry air becomes an ordinary Langmuir isotherm in humid air (J Chem Phys 2024, breakthrough experiments plus lattice kinetic theory; read at abstract level). The related mmen-Mg2(dobpdc) is stable only up to 50% RH and needs 120 C under vacuum or 150 C under N2 to regenerate (Chem Sci 2023, doi 10.1039/d3sc02554c, full text). Cooperative binding therefore does not yet deliver its roughly 1.1 GJ/t sensible-heat advantage in real air.

surprises: The 2024 Nature charged-sorbent result, widely reported as low-energy, has an author-estimated electrical demand of 6.5-11.4 GJ/t, worse than incumbent plants. OptiLex reproduces both numbers as pure sensible heat from the 0.08-0.14 mol/kg capacity, and humidity (11% to 38% RH) nearly halves the capacity.

The photo-DAC authors themselves calculate a theoretical minimum of 7.7-8.8 GJ/t of UV light and call the energy requirement unsustainable; the experiment ran at 1 mM concentration with 24 h loading and 5 days of dark release per cycle.

Humidity helps as often as it hurts: it removes the cooperative step in amine-appended MOFs and halves charged-sorbent capacity, but it more than doubles the amine aerogel's uptake (2.93 to 6.57 mmol/g) and is required for the TriH triamine to work at all at 20 C.
A simple molecular solid with no framework (TriH) holds the reported capacity record under DAC conditions (8.9 mmol/g), above every MOF, but melts at 50-52 C and evaporates during regeneration.

A 2026 claim of 0.94 GJ/t regeneration for a biphasic ionic liquid is below what the second law allows for a full cycle to pure CO2 with heat near 100 C (8.3 kJ/mol exergy supplied vs a 20.5 kJ/mol floor); it is probably a partial accounting or a dilute product. Abstract only, so the cause is unconfirmed.

No measured carbonic-anhydrase kinetics at 400 ppm CO2 turned up for 2022-2026; the durability data are at 10% CO2, and a 2026 paper titled for enzymatic DAC only screened membrane supports without enzyme.

The first long outdoor moisture-swing record (over 300 days) failed through UV damage, nitrate competition and biofouling, not through heat or oxidation, which are the failure modes most lab studies test.

An integrated electrochemical DAC cell needs 17.8-25.8 GJ/t when honestly paired with oxygen evolution, while component-level papers quote 1-3 GJ/t; the gap is the counter-reaction and capture efficiency of 40-50%.

Method limits: this session's WebSearch quota was exhausted, so literature was retrieved through the Europe PMC and Crossref APIs and open-access full texts. Coverage is good for ACS, Nature, Wiley and RSC journals and thin for Elsevier chemical-engineering journals and company white papers (Avnos, Verdox, RepAir, Holocene could not be checked beyond one company web page). Items marked not verified from primary rest on abstracts only. Calculation scripts: climate/runs/2026-10-06-sorbents/scripts/triggers_calc.py and climate/runs/2026-10-06-sorbents/scripts/sanity_claims.py.

If it replicates with a pure-CO2 product, raising capacity through 1:1 amine-to-CO2 stoichiometry is the most effective measured way to cut regeneration energy among the unconventional triggers.
verifs.corrected_claim: A defect-engineered, TEPA-grafted conductive graphene aerogel (N5-dGA; Shen et al., Nat Commun 17, 8885, published 21 July 2026) took up 6.57 mmol CO2/g at saturation from simulated air (400 ppm CO2 in N2, no O2) at 25 C and 80% RH, and 2.93 mmol/g dry. This was measured on a 65 mg packed bed. It was regenerated by Joule heating (0.6 A, about 80 C) under a dry argon sweep, so the product was dilute CO2. The 3.4 GJ/t "heat duty" is a thermodynamic component sum (reaction enthalpy, sensible heats, water desorption; no heat recovery). Its experimental check is electrical work minus estimated heat loss, so it is not gross electricity delivered. Uptake fell 3.7% by cycle 100 (6.57 to 6.33 mmol/g) and was then flat to 500 cycles, all in O2-free gas. This is a single multi-institution study with no independent replication. The 1:1 amine-to-CO2 stoichiometry was shown only in pure CO2 (12.6 mmol/g, reported as 1.1:1). The paper does not show that the capacity gain is what lowers regeneration energy: its own comparison table lists another Joule-heated sorbent at 3.5-3.7 GJ/t with only 2.4 mmol/g. The statement that this is "the most effective measured way to cut regeneration energy among the unconventional triggers" is therefore not supported by this source.
verifs.caveats:
All headline numbers match the primary source (main text, Supplementary Information and peer review file, read directly). The context below changes how the claim can be used.

1. **Not real air.** The feed was CO2/N2 (0.04/99.96) at 1000 mL/min through a 4.6 mm ID quartz tube. A reviewer raised hot-spot oxidation of the grafted amines; the authors replied only that they will look at oxygen stability in future. The 100- and 500-cycle results say nothing about oxidative degradation, the main failure mode for amine sorbents.

2. **The 3.4 GJ/t is net thermal, not electrical input.** Rebuilding it from Supplementary Table 2 gives about 3.36 GJ/t:
   - CO2 desorption at 60.7 kJ/mol: 1.38
   - quartz column sensible heat: about 1.30 (a bench artifact; the column weighs 10.4 times the sample)
   - sorbent sensible heat: about 0.30
   - water desorption: about 0.30
   - CO2 and water sensible heat: about 0.08

   The experimental value subtracts a Fourier-law heat-loss estimate from the electrical work. Using the Table S3 parameters, my estimate of that loss term (about 0.68 W) is the same size as the 0.64 W average input, so the validation is a small difference between two large numbers. Gross electricity per tonne at this scale is probably tens of GJ/t or more (my estimate, not stated in the paper). Vacuum, compression and CO2 concentration energy are excluded. The techno-economic analysis adds 0.99 GJ/t for auxiliaries, and the $48-62/t figure is projected variable OPEX at an assumed 4000 t/yr, not a measured cost.

3. **Water penalty rests on one low number.** The paper assumes 0.13 g H2O per g CO2 at 80% RH (about 0.3 mol H2O per mol CO2), taken from a single competitive breakthrough run. A higher co-adsorption would raise the heat duty materially.

4. **1:1 stoichiometry is not demonstrated at 400 ppm.** Scaling the paper's own pure-CO2 figure (12.6 mmol/g = 1.1:1), the 400 ppm uptakes correspond to roughly 0.47 CO2 per amine humid and 0.21 dry (my calculation). That is at or below the conventional 0.5 limit. The proton-trap mechanism is supported by DFT/AIMD, EPR and pure-CO2 uptake.

5. **Capacity only reduces the sensible-heat terms.** The reaction enthalpy (1.38 GJ/t) is unaffected by capacity. The authors themselves attribute the low heat duty to direct Joule heating and field-assisted desorption, not to stoichiometry.

6. **Uptake is a saturation value.** 6.57 mmol/g was reached after about 1700 min/g of adsorption (roughly 110 minutes for the bed); the C/C0 = 0.95 value is 6.41. The "28.8% above record" comparison is against 5.1 mmol/g for Polyam-N-Cu2+.

7. **Volumetric capacity is very low.** The paper reports 52.6 mol/m3 (about 2.3 kg CO2 per m3) against 777 mol/m3 for Lewatit VP OC 1065, a point a reviewer called a likely commercial limitation. The 52.6 figure matches the 8 mg/cm3 bare-aerogel density, not the 27 mg/cm3 stated for N5-dGA, so the paper is internally inconsistent here.

8. **Synthesis is at 20 mg batch scale.** It uses a 1600 C anneal and Ar plasma at 700 C; a reviewer flagged the plasma step as expensive and poorly scalable.

9. **"Single group" is loosely accurate.** Authors span Zhejiang University of Technology, Zhejiang University, Baima Lake Laboratory, Hangzhou Normal University and UCL, but it is one study.

The WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted, so I did not check for independent replications or post-publication critiques.

Sources: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-75916-7 ; Supplementary Information (41467_2026_75916_MOESM1_ESM.pdf) ; Peer Review file (41467_2026_75916_MOESM2_ESM.pdf).

verifs.corrected_claim: For one diamine-appended MOF, 2-ampd-(Mg,Mn)2(dobpdc), Marshall et al. (J. Chem. Phys. 161, 184703, Nov 2024; ExxonMobil; arXiv 2407.16879) measured breakthrough curves with 400 ppm CO2 in humid N2 at 22 C and 0-75% RH. Humidity increased both CO2 equilibrium capacity and adsorption rate, and removed the dry-gas induction effect. Their lattice kinetic theory fits the data by postulating (not directly observing) that co-adsorbed water screens the ion-pair attraction and shifts CO2 from cooperative ammonium-carbamate chains to non-cooperative singles. A model prediction, not a measured humid isotherm, is that the dry step (Type V) isotherm becomes Langmuir-like (Type I) at high humidity. In the model the adsorbed phase is nearly 100% non-cooperative only at 50% and 75% RH (above water pore filling); at 36% RH and below, cooperative chains still dominate at long times. Separately, for a different diamine, mmen-Mg2(dobpdc), Bose et al. (Chem. Sci. 2023, 14, 9380, measured) report it "is stable up to 50% relative humidity when the adsorption temperature varies from 25-40 C" and that "the best regeneration condition can be achieved at 120 C under dynamic vacuum and at 150 C under N2"; CO2 uptake at 400 ppm and 25 C was 1.5 mmol/g dry and about 1.7 mmol/g at 50% RH (with about 3 mmol/g H2O co-adsorbed). Neither paper quantifies a regeneration-energy penalty or mentions a 1.1 GJ/t sensible-heat figure. The statement that cooperative binding fails to deliver its energy advantage in real air is the claim author's inference, not a finding of either source.
verifs.caveats:
How I checked: Crossref abstract plus the full arXiv preprint (2407.16879) for the JCP paper; Europe PMC abstract and full-text XML (PMC10498709) for the Chem Sci paper. The publisher pages returned 403, and the Chem Sci body details came through a summarizing fetch, so treat them as less firm than the abstract quotes.

What changes the claim's use:

1. **The humidity effect is positive for uptake.** The JCP paper says "The presence of humidity increases both CO2 adsorption capacity and kinetics" (an appendix humid TGA at 60% RH gives about 2.57 mmol/g). The paper calls the loss of the step a matter with "significant ramifications on the design and modelling" of DAC processes; it does not call it a penalty. Any energy disadvantage would come from the desorption side (a Langmuir isotherm needs a larger swing), which the paper does not study.

2. **The mechanism is inferred, not observed.** The cooperative-to-non-cooperative shift is a postulate justified by a dielectric-screening argument and fitted with two empirical constants (c1 = 50, c2 = 1200). There is no spectroscopic confirmation and no measured humid equilibrium isotherm. The paper also notes the theory overpredicts at 25% RH and underpredicts at 36% RH.

3. **Measurement conditions are narrower than "humid air".** One material (2-ampd, which shows a two-step isotherm), 400 ppm CO2 in N2 rather than real air, 22 C, a single packed bed, and no cycling or durability data. The full loss of cooperativity is modelled only at 50% RH and above. Generalizing to all diamine-appended MOFs is an extrapolation.

4. **mmen-Mg2(dobpdc) is a different diamine from the JCP material.** Calling it "related" is fair, but the 50% RH limit and regeneration temperatures do not transfer to 2-ampd variants.

5. **The Chem Sci evidence base is thin.** Humid cycling was only 10 cycles, on a sample that was 50-60% aminated. At 45-50% RH the total (CO2 + H2O) uptake already fell about 15%, while at 25-30% RH there was no loss. The instability evidence above 50% RH is an accelerated aging test (80% RH, 70 C, 12 h) that stripped the amine and cut uptake from 1.5 to 0.07 mmol/g; re-amination restored it, so the failure is diamine loss, not framework collapse. "Stable only up to 50% RH" is therefore the abstract's wording, not a sharply measured threshold.

6. **"Needs" overstates the regeneration finding.** The paper reports 120 C vacuum and 150 C N2 as the best conditions found, not minimum requirements. The body reportedly also states full regeneration at 100 C for four hours under dynamic vacuum. N2 purge regeneration does not produce concentrated CO2, so it is not a DAC-relevant product condition; regeneration under 100% CO2 at 150 C lost capacity over 50 cycles.

7. **The 1.1 GJ/t figure has no source here.** It must be traced to its own origin (likely a process-model estimate) before use. Combining it with these two papers into "does not yet deliver" is a plausible hypothesis, not a measured result.
